Image 5 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: a classroom on the yard side of ZŠ Sokolíkova 2 in Bratislava-Dúbravka, a typified Czechoslovak school opened in 1974. Image 2 is a real classroom of that period (a two-panel green chalkboard on the front wall, a light wooden teacher's table, two-seat pupils' desks and chairs on steel frames); image 3 is a real Czechoslovak classroom (desks and chairs with green steel frames, wooden tops and plywood seats, a chalk tray under the board). Paint the furniture, board and materials from them, but NOT their cameras, their portraits, banners, posters, name cards, TV sets or projectors. Image 4 is the real 12-storey panel tower block on Galbavého street about 150 m north of the school: it stands in the distance in the window view, above the trees, in its original plain grey-and-white panel finish (no coloured cladding).

Brief: an after-school club in the classroom on Thursday 15 June 1995 at about half past three in the afternoon - not a normal lesson: the green chalkboard, the pupils' desks pushed together on the right with children's drawings and hand-drawn paper maps on them, a paper wall map on a roller, the teacher's table with a portable cassette tape recorder and a small microphone on a stand. The walls are one plain soft yellow colour with a slightly darker yellow-ochre glossy dado (no murals, no pictures painted on walls). The windows face the school's sports yard on the north-east, so no direct sun comes in: the classroom is filled with soft, warm, bright summer daylight, while outside the yard lies in full afternoon sunshine.

Camera: one-point perspective exactly as in the sketch. The camera stands at the back of the classroom about 2.2 m high and looks straight at the front wall, which is parallel to the picture; vertical lines stay vertical; the horizon is at y 352. In front of the left half of the board stands the light wooden teacher's table; on it a grey portable cassette tape recorder, a small black microphone on a little stand and a few papers. On the right half of the room two rows of two-seat pupils' desks pushed together side by side (light wooden tops on green tubular steel frames) with green-framed plywood chairs on the near side, loose children's drawings and hand-drawn paper maps lying on the desks. The right wall is one long ribbon window with white-painted wooden mullions, a light stone sill and white radiators under it; through the glass the sunny sports yard of the school: green lawn, a reddish clay athletics track, a fenced multi-sport court, tall poplars and limes, and in the distance the four-storey panel blocks and the tall grey-and-white panel tower.
